item.title: Yuzawa Snow Country: Ski Resorts Reachable Direct from the Shinkansen — Guide
item.description: Yuzawa is Japan’s most accessible ski region for visitors without a car, thanks to GALA Yuzawa resort’s unique gondola station built directly into Echigo-Yuzawa Shinkansen Station, allowing skiers to travel from central Tokyo to the slopes in under 90 minutes with minimal transfers. The town, part of the ‘snow country’ immortalised in Nobel laureate Yasunari Kawabata’s novel of the same name, hosts numerous resorts of varying difficulty across the surrounding mountains, along with hot springs that make an ideal post-ski relaxation stop.

item.title: Inaniwa Udon: Akita's Silky Handmade Noodles — Guide
item.description: Inaniwa udon, from Akita’s Yuzawa region, is one of Japan’s three great udon alongside Sanuki and Mizusawa — distinguished by its extraordinarily thin, silky-smooth strands made through a laborious multi-day hand-stretching process. Served cold in summer with dipping broth, or warm in a clear dashi, it is a study in refined simplicity. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Yuzawa (Inaniwa), Akita Hours Restaurant hours Admission ~¥900–1,500 a bowl Time needed About 45 min Best time Year-round; cold in summer What to Try Extraordinarily thin, silky-smooth udon strands.

item.title: Best Hotels & Ryokan in Niigata: Yuzawa, Sado Island & Niigata City
item.description: Niigata Prefecture faces the Sea of Japan and produces Japan’s finest rice (Uonuma Koshihikari) and some of the country’s most celebrated sake. The prefecture spans from the ski resorts of Echigo-Yuzawa (accessible from Tokyo in 70 minutes by Shinkansen) to the ancient cultural island of Sado — Japan’s sixth-largest island, once a place of exile for emperors and artists. Best Areas to Stay Echigo-Yuzawa — Ski & Onsen Resort A famous ski resort town at the foot of the Echigo mountains — 70 minutes from Tokyo Station by Shinkansen.
